workflow_metadata.description: Use reflow_gap_closure.py (matrix transformation + SVD) to infer System D (sample) properties
workflow_metadata.purpose: Transform DAG to matrices, apply SVD-based gap closure, generate hypotheses for System D properties, validate scientific plausibility

workflow_steps.description: Transform experimental system DAG to matrices for mathematical inference

actions.details: Read experimental_system_architecture.json and experimental_system_graph.json from working memory paths
Create adjacency matrix A[i,j] = 1 if edge from node i to node j exists, 0 otherwise. Rows/cols = [System A, System B, System C, System D, System E]
Create measurement matrix B encoding OBSERVED interactions. B[i,j] = observability (HIGH=1.0, MEDIUM=0.5, LOW=0.1) if edge i→j is measured. Focus on D→E (sample→detector) edges.
actions.output: Measurement matrix B (N×N or M×N where M = # of measurements)

actions.details: Create property matrix P encoding KNOWN system properties. P[i,j] = interaction_strength if edge i→j has KNOWN properties (Systems A, B, C, E). P[d,j] = UNKNOWN for System D rows.
actions.output: Property matrix P (N×N with unknowns for System D)

actions.details: Create docs/matrix_transformation.md: matrix dimensions, encoding schemes, known vs unknown elements, mathematical formulation (B = P × A or similar)

criteria: System D elements identified as unknowns

workflow_steps.description: Apply SVD-based gap closure to infer System D properties

actions.details: Run gap closure integration wrapper. Internally calls matrix_gap_detection.py (SVD solver) and link_architectures.py (architecture linking).
Check that gap_closure_proposals.json exists and contains proposals for System D properties
Extract: (1) SVD singular values (condition number), (2) Inferred System D properties, (3) Confidence scores, (4) Alternative hypotheses

criteria: At least one proposal for System D

workflow_steps.description: Interpret SVD singular values and assess inference quality

actions.details: Check SVD singular values (σ1, σ2, ..., σn): (1) Large singular values → strong constraints, (2) Small singular values → weak constraints, (3) Condition number κ = σ_max/σ_min (if κ >> 1, problem is ill-conditioned)
Properties corresponding to large singular values are well-constrained by measurements. Example: If σ1 is large and corresponds to 'lattice parameter a', then 'a' is well-determined.
Properties corresponding to small singular values are under-constrained. Example: If σ_n is tiny and corresponds to 'crystal orientation', orientation is poorly determined.
Overall confidence based on: (1) Condition number (κ < 100 is good), (2) Ratio of well-constrained to total properties, (3) Number of measurements vs unknowns

workflow_steps.description: Translate gap closure proposals into testable scientific hypotheses

actions.details: From gap_closure_proposals.json, extract inferred values for System D properties. Example: crystal_structure='FCC', lattice_parameter_a='3.92 Å', space_group='Fm-3m'
Formulate primary hypothesis based on highest-confidence proposals. Example: 'Hypothesis 1: Sample is an FCC crystal with lattice parameter a=3.92±0.05 Å, space group Fm-3m.'
If multiple plausible solutions exist (degeneracy), generate alternative hypotheses. Example: 'Hypothesis 2: Sample could also be HCP with c/a=1.63.'
For each hypothesis, identify testable predictions. Example: 'If FCC Fm-3m, then diffraction peaks should appear at 2θ = 38.5°, 44.7°, 65.1° (Cu Kα).'
Create docs/scientific_hypotheses.md: primary hypothesis, alternative hypotheses, testable predictions, confidence levels, experimental validation plan

workflow_steps.description: Validate gap closure proposals for physical plausibility

actions.details: Verify inferred properties obey physical laws: (1) Positive energies, (2) Lattice parameters > 0, (3) Physically realizable crystal structures, (4) Reasonable material properties
actions.validation: All proposals physically plausible (WARN if violations)

actions.details: If sample type is partially known (e.g., 'oxide'), compare inferred properties to known materials databases (e.g., ICSD, Materials Project). Flag if no match found.
Verify inferred properties are internally consistent. Example: If space group is centrosymmetric, but structure has asymmetric atomic positions, flag inconsistency.
Present hypotheses to user for expert review. Ask: Do these hypotheses make physical sense for your sample?

workflow_steps.description: Propose follow-up experiments to validate hypotheses

actions.details: What additional measurements would distinguish between hypotheses? Example: If Hypothesis 1 (FCC) vs Hypothesis 2 (HCP), measure {111} vs {002} peak intensities.
What other experimental techniques would validate inferred properties? Example: XRD infers structure → validate with TEM, Raman, or neutron diffraction.
Rank validation experiments by: (1) Confidence gain, (2) Experimental feasibility, (3) Cost/time
Create docs/validation_experiment_plan.md: discriminating measurements, complementary techniques, prioritized validation plan, expected outcomes

workflow_steps.description: Synthesize all results into comprehensive scientific report

actions.details: Create docs/GAP_CLOSURE_REPORT.md with sections: (1) Experimental system summary, (2) Matrix transformation, (3) SVD analysis, (4) Inferred properties, (5) Hypotheses, (6) Validation plan
Create: (1) Before/after diagrams (System D UNKNOWN → System D inferred), (2) SVD singular value plot, (3) Hypothesis comparison table
Export inferred System D properties to: (1) JSON (specs/machine/gap_closure/inferred_system_d.json), (2) CSV for analysis, (3) LaTeX table for publication
Save complete workflow state: architectures, graphs, matrices, proposals, hypotheses, validation plan. Timestamp all artifacts.

workflow_steps.description: Finalize gap closure analysis and provide next steps

actions.details: Set workflow_status='completed', current_workflow=null, completion_date=<timestamp>
Create docs/workflow_completion_summary.md: workflows executed, key results, inferred System D properties, hypotheses generated, validation plan, next steps

Present to user: (1) Inferred System D properties, (2) Generated hypotheses, (3) Recommended validation experiments, (4) Invitation to iterate (refine measurements, update architecture, re-run gap closure)
Ask user: 'Would you like to: (1) Refine the experimental system model? (2) Add more measurements? (3) Update System D constraints? (4) Re-run gap closure analysis?'

quality_gates.description: Verify gap closure analysis produced valid, plausible results

iteration_support.description: Scientific discovery is iterative - users may want to refine and re-run gap closure
iteration_actions: Add more measurements (new System E components)
Refine System D constraints (change UNKNOWN to PARTIALLY_KNOWN)
